aliases: Proposed Microsoft Data Center in Kenosha
status_detail: City FAQ says Microsoft proposed a data center on a 242-acre site north of Highway 142 and east of County Highway MB, purchased in early 2025; the project remains in early planning and must complete site-plan/building-permit processes. City announcement says ordinances to attach and rezone the approximately 240-acre site were unanimously passed in December 2024, paving the way for potential datacenter development. Capacity is inferred as at least 100 MW because the City FAQ ties PSC very-large-user rate discussion to projects requiring 100 MW or more; no final facility MW was published in the official materials reviewed.
notes: Official city/county evidence confirms Microsoft land purchase and proposed data center. FAQ states no TIF or incentives, Microsoft funds required infrastructure, municipal water connection, closed-loop liquid cooling expected, NDA terminated June 22, 2026, and permitting was not complete as of the FAQ.

project_name: Cloverleaf Infrastructure Carlton data center complex
aliases: Kewaunee Power Station area data center
status_detail: Town of Carlton special meeting minutes dated August 13, 2025 state Cloverleaf Infrastructure was looking to acquire about 800 acres in Carlton for a data center complex of about 100 MW. Wisconsin Watch reported January 21, 2026 that Town of Carlton and Cloverleaf officials confirmed Cloverleaf was no longer pursuing the project near Kewaunee Power Station after local opposition, with the resolution occurring in late 2025.
notes: Official town meeting minutes provide the original project details; later news confirms withdrawal/no longer pursuing. EnergySolutions/Kewaunee nuclear-power restart is related power-market context, not itself a data center project.

project_name: Potential Manitowoc County data center land assembly
aliases: Two Rivers-Mishicot-Two Creeks data center concern
city: Mishicot / Two Rivers / Two Creeks area
status_detail: Town of Two Rivers official data-center page says Two Rivers, Mishicot and Two Creeks sent resolutions to Manitowoc County Planning and Zoning requesting a moratorium on data center applications. FOX 11 reported the three towns acted after several Mishicot farms were approached with land purchase offers by Cloverleaf Infrastructure and NSI Land Services. WPR reported the county board approved an 18-month moratorium on April 28, 2026 and that no formal proposals had yet been received.
notes: Recorded as a potential/early land-assembly lead rather than an approved project because available official/news evidence describes approaches to landowners and a moratorium, not a filed application. Community site claims developers sought up to 6,000 acres, but that is advocacy/source-low evidence.
